clue.text: Notice that's best put up

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting a word up means reading it from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: the tops are the best of something

explanation.surface: A remark that something is best displayed prominently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' turns TOPS upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To spot something is to notice it, an ordinary synonym for seeing.

clue.text: Line in art, in a manner of speaking

indicators.note: the letter for line goes inside the word for the art

parts.note: drawing is an art form

explanation.surface: A remark about a line in a picture, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a manner of speaking' looks like a stock phrase; its first 'in' is just a link and 'a manner of speaking' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawl is a slow, lazy way of talking, so drawling is a speaking style.

clue.text: Smart little bird, not fully-fledged

indicators.note: the bird's word is not complete: its final letter is cut off

parts.note: a chick is a baby bird

explanation.surface: A young bird looking smart though its feathers are not fully grown.
explanation.definitionFit: Chic means stylish or elegant, a synonym of smart in the sense of well dressed.

clue.text: Single us out for unfair appearance?

indicators.note: the letters are sent out of their order, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Someone protests at being unfairly picked out from the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges SINGLEUS; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Ugliness is an appearance that is not fair, using fair in its old sense of beautiful.

clue.text: Memorable impression of German comic

indicators.note: something comic is played about with, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A lasting memory left by a German comedian.
explanation.definitionFit: An engram is a hypothetical trace a memory leaves in the brain, a memorable impression.

clue.text: Chinese citizens last in boot camp

parts.note: Canton, the old name of the Chinese city Guangzhou, stands in for something Chinese
citizens are men, the people of a place

indicators.note: the final letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: Chinese people bringing up the rear at a military training camp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boot camp' looks like one phrase, but 'boot' only supplies its last letter T and 'camp' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantonment is a military station or encampment, especially in former British India.

clue.text: Man in the Circus :-)

definitions.meaning: George ... is John le Carré's spy, working for the Circus, his nickname for British intelligence headquarters
this emoticon of a happy face is called by this name

explanation.walkthrough: The Circus is not a big top: in le Carré's novels it is the nickname of MI6.
explanation.definitionFit: The fictional spy George Smiley works in the Circus, and a grinning face emoticon is also called this.

clue.text: Remarkable gift on back of lorry for 1

parts.note: ESP, extrasensory perception, is an extraordinary gift

indicators.note: the final letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: A remarkable present tied on the back of a lorry.
explanation.walkthrough: '1' refers to the answer of 1-down, SPOT.
explanation.definitionFit: To espy is to catch sight of, the same as to spot.

clue.text: Forward march ending somewhere in Australia

parts.note: forward can mean cheeky or pert

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word before is used

explanation.surface: A military march ending its route in an Australian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Perth is the capital city of Western Australia.

clue.text: Police needing information women provided about ringleader

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

indicators.note: the women's word goes around the letter for the leader

parts.note: dames are women
the leader, or first letter, of ring is R

explanation.surface: The police have needed tips from women about the boss of a gang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ringleader' is split: the leader of 'ring' is its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Gendarmes are French police officers, so collectively they are police.

clue.text: Old newsman involved in row with cretin

indicators.note: involved suggests the letters are tangled together into a new order

explanation.surface: A traditional announcer caught up in an argument with an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: Before newspapers, a town crier called out public announcements in the streets, a bringer of news.

clue.text: 100% wanting to score

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the following word is removed

parts.note: totally means one hundred per cent, completely
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone fully committed to scoring a goal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting' takes TO out of TOTALLY.
explanation.definitionFit: A tally is a running score or count of points.

clue.text: Earthenware mug — one with short measure inside

indicators.note: these letters are placed within the word for the mug

parts.note: mug is slang for face
I is the Roman numeral for one
an en is a small printing measure, half an em

explanation.surface: A pottery cup, with a short measure of drink poured into it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mug' looks like a cup but is slang for a face.
explanation.definitionFit: Faience is a type of glazed earthenware or pottery.

clue.text: Entering wood where Geordies are not so thick

indicators.note: the place letters go inside the word for the wood

parts.note: fir is a timber, a kind of wood
Geordies come from Newcastle, in the north-east of England, abbreviated NE

explanation.surface: Walking into a forest in the north-east where the trees grow less densely.
explanation.walkthrough: Geordies are people from Newcastle upon Tyne, in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Finer means thinner or more slender, the comparative of fine as opposed to coarse.

clue.text: How Rover may greet acquaintance in a jam?

definitions.meaning: dogs meeting sniff each other, one's snout at the other's rear
cars stuck in a traffic jam sit close bumper to bumper

explanation.walkthrough: Rover is a stock name for a pet dog.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes dogs sniffing each other and also queued cars bumper to bumper in traffic.

clue.text: Male getting on looked well off

parts.note: taken as written
eyed means looked at

explanation.surface: An older man looked prosperous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting on' suggests ageing, but 'getting' is a link and 'on' stands as written.
explanation.definitionFit: Moneyed means wealthy, having plenty of money.

clue.text: Research key provided by centre in Slovenia

parts.note: Del is the delete key on a keyboard

indicators.note: the middle letters of the next word are taken

explanation.surface: Key research funded by a centre in Slovenia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre in' picks the middle pair VE from Slovenia.
explanation.definitionFit: To delve is to dig deeply into a subject, to research it.

clue.text: Hot drink, say, consumed by North American

indicators.note: the example letters are swallowed up by the letters for North American

parts.note: eg, for example, is what say can mean

explanation.surface: A hot beverage drunk by someone from North America.
explanation.definitionFit: Negus is a hot drink of port or sherry with sugar, lemon and spice.

clue.text: Notes from Jamaica in Das Kapital

indicators.note: the letters are found inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Musical notes from the Caribbean appear in Marx's work.
explanation.definitionFit: Ska is a style of popular music that began in Jamaica.

clue.text: Is red man possibly Sioux?

indicators.note: possibly suggests another arrangement of these letters

explanation.surface: Asking whether a red-faced man could be a Native American.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is by example, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sioux are one group of American Indian peoples, the old term Amerinds.

clue.text: Stand while catching fish? On the contrary!

indicators.note: the surface says the word for while catches the fish
the catching runs the other way round, so the fish's word holds the other

parts.note: an eel is a fish
as can mean while

explanation.surface: Standing while trying to catch a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catching' would have the while word hold the fish; 'On the contrary!' flips which piece holds which.
explanation.definitionFit: An easel is a stand for holding a painting or board.

clue.text: Larks in a strange land

indicators.note: strange suggests these letters are set out oddly into a new order

explanation.surface: Songbirds flying in a foreign country.
explanation.definitionFit: Sri Lanka is an island country in the Indian Ocean.

clue.text: Was a speaker heard in another place?

indicators.note: the clue's word is listened to rather than read, giving one that sounds the same

parts.note: resited means located somewhere else

explanation.surface: Asking whether someone was heard speaking somewhere else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in another place' is also the House of Lords in Commons usage, adding to the political surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To recite is to say aloud from memory, so one who recited was speaking.

clue.text: US network incorporating odd fragments

indicators.note: the outer word takes the other one into its body

parts.note: CBS is an American TV network
rum means odd or strange

explanation.surface: An American broadcaster airing bits of odd material.
explanation.definitionFit: Crumbs are tiny fragments, especially of bread.

clue.text: Dirty passage

explanation.definitionFit: To defile is to soil or pollute, and a defile is a narrow gorge through mountains.

clue.text: Lace drink after man scratched head

indicators.note: the drink comes after the other piece
the first letter of the word is scratched out

parts.note: gent is short for gentleman, a man
wine is a drink

explanation.surface: Someone laces a drink after a man scratches his head.
explanation.definitionFit: To lace things together is to twist or weave them, to entwine.

clue.text: Certain people don't do this but do otherwise

indicators.note: otherwise means arranged differently, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A paradoxical remark about what sure people avoid doing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Certain' means sure: those who are certain do not have misgivings.
explanation.definitionFit: To doubt is to be uncertain, the opposite of being sure.

clue.text: Far from gay, missing first bouquet

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is lost

parts.note: a wine's bouquet is its odour

explanation.surface: Someone sad at missing out on the first bunch of flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bouquet' suggests flowers, but means a smell.
explanation.definitionFit: Dour means stern and gloomy, far from cheerful.

clue.text: Big name in history of film projection almost outside hotel

definitions.text: Big name in history of film

indicators.note: the shortened word goes around the hotel
the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a flange is a projecting rim
the Ritz is a famous London hotel

explanation.surface: A celebrated director's movie projected outside a hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'projection' suggests the cinema, but it is a flange.
explanation.definitionFit: Fritz Lang was the Austrian-German director of Metropolis and M, a giant of cinema history.

clue.text: He wrote about a large weight

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the pieces read backwards

parts.note: oz, an ounce, is a weight

explanation.surface: A writer composing a piece about a heavy weight.
explanation.definitionFit: Emile Zola was a French novelist, a man who wrote.

clue.text: Boxer, for example, turning up with second in gallery

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up reads the word from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: a boxer is a breed of dog

explanation.surface: A boxer appearing in a gallery with his second.
explanation.walkthrough: The gods are the highest gallery in a theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: The gods are the cheap upper gallery seats in a theatre, near the ceiling.

clue.text: Rampant Dubliner recollected Dedalus at first

indicators.note: recollected read as re-collected means gathered again in a new order
only the first letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: A Dubliner wildly remembers Stephen Dedalus, Joyce's hero.
explanation.definitionFit: Unbridled means unrestrained, the same as rampant.

clue.text: Popular song about weekend

indicators.note: the song's word goes around the letter

parts.note: a lied is a German art song
the end of week is its last letter K

explanation.surface: A popular song about the weekend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'weekend' is read as week's end, its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something liked is popular, favoured by people.
